findings.problem: Both proofs run the same argument. They take the archComponent of glArch β at w, check that its (1,0) entry vanishes using glArch_apply and h10, and apply the unit-diagonal lemma. They then prove two entry-identification equalities e0 and e1 (lines 721-728 and 1056-1063) and rewrite them into h. The 15-line block is copied; only the target form of the diagonal entries differs, which is (β i i).1 w in one place and archUnitAt w (borelDiagFst ..) in the other. These are definitionally the same, as the rfl steps show.
findings.proposed_change: Prove one lemma before both uses, for example norm_arch_diag_of_mem_maximalCompact (β) (hβ : β ∈ adelicBorel ..) (hβK : β ∈ adelicMaximalCompact K) (w) : ‖((β : Matrix ..) 0 0).1 w‖ = 1 ∧ ‖((β : Matrix ..) 1 1).1 w‖ = 1. Its proof is the current harch body. Then harch is `fun w => this β hβ hβK w`. The extensionEmbedding lemma becomes the same fact, transported with the isometry iso (line 1065) and `show` to the archUnitAt form, so its e0/e1/h10/hk steps disappear.
findings.benefit: The archimedean diagonal computation is stated and proved once. Both consumers shrink to a few lines, and any change to glArch/archComponent unfolding is made in one place.

findings.problem: borelDiag_integral and the hfin block of distribHaarChar_borelDiag_eq_one (lines 735-743) both start from valued_finComponent_apply_le_one. Each then proves the same two identifications, ex (the finComponent entry equals (β i i).2 v) and ey (the inverse entry equals (β⁻¹ i i).2 v), and rewrites them into the bound. So the local integrality bounds for β and β⁻¹ at v are derived twice. The earlier copy then still has to rebuild the unit-norm statement by hand. borelDiag_integral already supplies exactly these facts for borelDiagFst and borelDiagSnd.
findings.proposed_change: Extract a lemma, for example valued_diag_entries_le_one (hβK : β ∈ adelicMaximalCompact K) (v) (i : Fin 2) : Valued.v ((β i i).2 v) ≤ 1 ∧ Valued.v ((β⁻¹ i i).2 v) ≤ 1, whose proof is the ex/ey/rw block. Define it before distribHaarChar_borelDiag_eq_one. Then hfin reduces to this lemma plus the existing hprodv and norm_eq_one_of_mul_eq_one. borelDiag_integral becomes two applications of it plus mem_adicCompletionIntegers, or hfin can use borelDiag_integral directly if that lemma is moved earlier.
findings.benefit: The entry-identification boilerplate (about 8 lines) appears once. The unit-norm lemma and the integrality lemma visibly rest on the same fact, so they no longer risk diverging.
